cover.prose:
The source image — an isometric block city over a strategy-breeding harness — works because of three quiet decisions, and only one of them is the city: it maps roles in a mechanism rather than files; it spends its one visual scalar (height) on a true quantity; and it keeps a CONDITION field that says what is currently wrong. This set keeps those three decisions and lets everything else change with altitude.

The result is an argument about form: a loop where there is a genuine cycle (sheet 1), panels where packages are too small to be cities (sheet 2), the full city where the measurement thesis is actually true (sheet 3), a massed spine where the family shares one core but the limbs never touch (sheet 4), a chart where edges would be fiction (sheet 5), and mostly prose where only a definition survives (sheet 6). Fitness peaks in the middle altitudes and collapses at both ends.

Above the sixth altitude the set stops arguing about form and starts measuring. Sheets 7–10 are a survey quartet, each counting the same subject at a different boundary: what the repository holds (the monorepo by mass), what npm delivers (the sample app's node_modules, 243× the app it serves), what the browser downloads (the docs deploy on the wire, where the prerendered prose tops the skyline and the lettering alone outweighs every routed app the site demonstrates), and who occupies the bytes after tree-shaking (the machine the router wraps is 21.0% of the bundle; the router itself, 6.5%). Sheet 11 cuts the same wire the other way, pricing 12 package quarters and 36 doors one at a time. Sheet 12 leaves the wire and draws the monorepo as its own CI reads it, the pull-request task graph punched onto a register plate. Sheet 13 ages the city by commit date, and sheet 14 draws it among the commons it builds on: the pull requests, issues and bug reports in other projects that its own record cites, sent or watched, and the home work that cites them. Sheet 1A brings sheet 1's document down to one page at reading size: the sample app's contacts view, measured in a browser and dimensioned the way a component drawing is. Interactive lanes (1i, 2B and 12i) walk the plates they sit beside, and the routed set stands sheets 2, 2C and 7 in the round. The appendix files plates whose subject is the atlas rather than the codebase: the sprite study behind the building sprites (appendix A1), and the survey office that turns the instrument on itself (appendix A2) — the census pipeline behind almost every number here, drawn as archive → probe stations → filed plates → drawings, introspected from the generator at build time, and walked live in its lane A2i. Appendix A3 turns sheet 7's ruler on the atlas itself: its drawing office, survey office, routed site and site build, massed beside the codebase they draw. Appendix A4 turns sheet 9's ruler on the atlas's own deploy: what the browser downloads from atlas.lit-ui-router.dev, district by district, beside the docs deploy summed by role. Appendix A5 draws the sheet every plate is set in as a dimensional drawing: its frame, head, plate, schedule, caption, notes and title block, measured in the built app and lettered in codes. Appendix A6 draws the atlas's own drawing rules broken, each incorrect use crossed beside its correct form at one scale and tied to the guard that catches it, or to none.

sheets.title: THE RENDER LOOP
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 1 — lit-ui-router 1.19.1 · the client circuit drawn as one isometric scene: every leg of the loop is a road on the grid, the document a browser window whose DOM rises in plates, and the six package entries a door strip along the footer · version read from census-files.json
sheets.caption: The loop sits on the ground: every leg is a road that turns along the iso axes and stops short of the wall it points at. The city breaks its metaphor once, on purpose — the document is not a building but a browser window whose DOM rises in plates. The core matches, the hall runs its hook bays, Lit commits onto a layer, and a click on the topmost plate flies back to location.
sheets.verdict: strong fit — the render cycle is a genuine circuit

sheets.title: THE DOCUMENT, DIMENSIONED
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 1 — ALTERNATE PLATE: sheet 1’s document at reading size — the sample app’s contacts page at /app/contacts/fruiz, measured in Chromium at 1280 and 390 wide and drawn as slots with chained codes, three details and the layer stack sheet 1 raises · rows read census-document.json @ 33cd7ce1, measured on the vanilla build at a61ce45e
sheets.caption: The contacts page of the sample app, drawn the way a dimensional drawing draws a component: the shell's nav, the named view it fills, the list that hugs its rows and the nested view that flexes beside it, every distance a code. At 390 the row wraps and the nested view drops under the list. The stack at the lower right is the page's layers from the window to the link, the plates sheet 1 raises.
sheets.verdict: alternate plate — sheet 1's document at reading size: the sample app's contacts page measured in Chromium, 25 rows in a list that hugs W1 beside a nested view that flexes and wraps under it at 390, one geometry for all four sample apps

sheets.title: THE RENDER LOOP, WALKED
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 1 — sheet 1's circuit, stepped · one navigation walked leg by leg · 10 STATIONS · 12 LEGS · 12 STEPS · surveyed at origin/main @ 33cd7ce1 (commit 2026-11-10)
sheets.caption: The circuit, stood up and stepped. 10 stations and 12 legs, then one click — a click on <a uiSref> from /people to /people/32 — walked in 12 steps under the pointer, every step standing on the 30 source lines the plate cites verbatim.
sheets.verdict: sheet 1's circuit with a pointer in it — 10 stations, 12 legs, and one click walked in 12 steps, every step standing on the source lines the plate cites verbatim

sheets.title: THE BRICK ASSEMBLY
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 2 — one baseplate, ten bricks, 104 authored files · an exploded LEGO assembly with every coupling named to the API call that makes it, brick and stud faces drawn opaque so nothing reads through a mass in front of it · REV J 2026-10-24: ui-router-registry takes schedule row 11, a compile-time part beside the lint plugin — types only, no stud, not drawn · source counted at origin/main @ 33cd7ce1 (2026-11-11)
sheets.caption: Every companion drawn here enters through a published stud — on @uirouter/core, or on a brick that publishes one of its own. Drawn exploded, the sheet answers the only question that matters about a plugin architecture: pull any brick off and what breaks? Only what stands on it or peers it — four bricks seat on lit-ui-router, one of them on the server too, three of them peering a brick on the plate — and the plate’s studs stay where they are.
sheets.verdict: exploded, then seated: every coupling is a published stud, on core or on the brick below — and the server takes none of core’s

sheets.title: THE COUPLING PLAN
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 2 — ALTERNATE PLATE: the ten companions sheet 2 schedules, laid out for reading — core central as a socket wall, companions at its right, the server below the no-DOM line — with every coupling drawn disengaged and lettered to its API call · rows read census-bricks.json @ 33cd7ce1
sheets.caption: The brick assembly, uncoupled and brought down to one elevation: core as a socket wall, companions as shallow blocks drawn just short of seated, and each of the six connection points on the wall — five published studs and one keyed red seat — large enough to letter its API call on the joint itself. Eight more joints are companion-to-companion, and one of those spans both halves of the plate.
sheets.verdict: alternate plate — the same joints at reading size: eight companion-to-companion joints from four companions, four of them two-armed, and ssr's arm bridges the flagship and the server across the no-DOM line

sheets.title: THE COUPLING BENCH
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 2 — INTERACTIVE PLATE: sheet 2A’s joints made live · 14 nodes in five columns, every tie a straight run · each of the 27 drawn edges is a published contract, with its declared range under the pointer
sheets.caption: The same assembly as sheets 2 and 2A, reduced to what a consumer's installer actually reads: 14 buildings and 27 contracts. Hover an edge for the range it declares and the section it lives in; hover a building for its version, what it declares, and what declares it.
sheets.verdict: 2A’s joints made live — every one of the 27 drawn edges is a published contract with its declared range under the pointer: 37 peers to 4 dependencies across the 12 packages, and no dependency is a router

sheets.caption: One box, eleven models. The sample apps, the docs site and the examples pin ten distinct sets of family parts, and the atlas’s own app pins an eleventh on its own branch; each set is drawn as the small assembly it makes on the runtime plates its parts peer, under a callout of its parts: effect, mobx and signal-polyfill share no model, no bricks stay in the box at the cabinet’s tree and no bricks with the atlas app, and one plate carries nothing at the cabinet’s tree and one with the atlas app.

sheets.title: THE INSTRUMENT YARD
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3 — 12 publishable packages · 31 tools · 102 turbo task names · one packer, many readers · every mass counted at origin/main @ 33cd7ce1 (2026-11-11) from www/atlas.lit-ui-router.dev/data/census-yard.json on scc Code lines — 431 authored files and 38,279 sloc across 18 massed structures, with the task-manager inset reading the same two plates sheet 3A draws
sheets.caption: The monorepo drawn as what it functionally is: a short conveyor that turns source into one tarball, inside a yard of instruments built to measure that tarball. Every structure carries its measured mass — footprint ∝ √sloc, height ∝ authored files — and gate severity is colour rather than height, because the two do not correlate: the blocks that stop the line are among the smallest on the sheet.

sheets.title: THE HANDOFF WORKS
sheets.sub: ALTITUDE 3 · ALTERNATE PLATE — the sheet-3 task-manager inset at full size: 9 of 14 workflows · 64 mise tasks in 5 homes · turbo ci 1508 nodes, 368 real · 4 seam types · 3 service doors · every frame sized to the widest DIN line it holds, so the spine is computed rather than hand-set · every count imported from www/atlas.lit-ui-router.dev/data/census-handoff.json + census-plate.json · counted at origin/main @ 33cd7ce1 (2026-11-11)
sheets.caption: The two task managers drawn as the two machines they are — mise the node-free umbrella, turbo the cached fan-out — with the seams as the featured parts: every crossing is a bolted gasket labeled with what crosses it and what the boundary buys. The star fitting is the cache gasket on the return duct: turbo caches mise, because the six re-entrant lint lanes hash the mise task files and mise.lock, so a tool-pin bump invalidates exactly its own lane.
